tasks.short: Provide formal and informal education to other staff

steps.what: Identify the actual staff learning need and intended teaching scope
Read the current approved protocol and select material appropriate to that need
Prepare the actual short teaching slides or handout using the selected content
Check the final material's clinical meaning, current protocol version and teaching suitability
Educate staff through explanation and demonstration using the checked material
Observe actual practice and clarify understanding with the staff learners

tasks.design: Configure the existing {DOCS} teaching template to reuse title styles, source references and standard layout for the actual material. Keep clinical selection, wording, final meaning review and staff instruction human; no patient data or generated clinical advice is introduced.
tasks.previous_blocker: Formatting an actual teaching aid consumes time alongside clinical preparation and staff instruction.
tasks.enabler_now: Native document styles and reusable source blocks remove layout work without generating a clinical procedure.
tasks.still_hard: Knowing what learners misunderstand and demonstrating safe practice.
tasks.human_edge: The nurse recognises uncertainty during practice and adjusts the explanation.
tasks.altitude: Less formatting of actual teaching aids; instructional responsibility and clinical authority remain unchanged.

reach.task: Prepare a short protocol-based staff teaching session
reach.learn: Teaching objectives, protocol version checks and supervised practice feedback

evidence.claim: Native document styles and reusable source blocks can reduce formatting of existing teaching aids without replacing clinical teaching. This is model knowledge.

assumptions: The focal role is the nurse providing an actual prepared staff session. It already uses a short slide set or handout. An informal bedside explanation without written material does not acquire a fictional handout or attendance record. All shares are E1 scenario estimates, not measured training baselines.

The clinical protocol owner supplies current document identifier, version, approved content and effective date. The nurse identifies the actual learning need in s1, reads sources in s2 and writes substantive content in s3. No transcript, automatic competency judgement or free content curation is assumed.

Three of fifteen preparation hours are title/source-block and layout work removed by the native template. Twelve retain actual clinical wording, source selection and correction. s4 retains all final clinical meaning checks. Ordinary author saving is included unchanged in s3, with no self-approval gate.

The material is used in the nurse's live session; no separate publication or email send is assumed. No training completion certificate, staff attendance registry or competency sign-off is invented. A real local credential or completion transaction needs its own actual capture and release steps.
unknowns: How often is a real written teaching aid used?
Are standard styles and source blocks already available?
Which sessions require a separate competency or completion record?
research_questions: Does the template remove actual formatting without shortening clinical preparation or learner practice?

already_counted.description: Full clinical meaning and protocol-version review

incremental.description: Maintain the actual teaching template and source blocks

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central removes three layout hours less 0.5 template upkeep: 2.5 net. Cautious case: an informal bedside explanation uses no written aid, or the existing template already handles layout; preserve that current route with no new template upkeep. All actual clinical explanation and practice remain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Collaborate with patients to plan future care and coordinate transitions or referrals

steps.what: Read current care needs, team decisions and the actual transition authorisation
Discuss future needs, preferences and practical concerns with the patient
Agree feasible next steps with the patient within the clinical team's plan
Write the actual agreed nursing transition plan in the patient record
Transfer existing verified patient and care fields into the receiving-provider handover draft
Write the case-specific handover narrative and unresolved care-coordination questions
Check the final handover meaning, authority, disclosure scope and exact receiving provider
Transmit the exact checked handover through the authorised secure provider channel
Save the ordinary internal nursing transition record

tasks.design: Use {OTHER}, the clinical record and secure referral exchange, to reuse verified existing fields in an inactive handover draft. Keep patient collaboration, the actual nursing plan and case-specific narrative human; transmit only the exact final handover and recipient checked by the nurse.
tasks.previous_blocker: The patient's agreed transition plan and existing identifiers are entered again for a receiving provider.
tasks.enabler_now: Native field reuse and a secure structured exchange can remove real second-entry and transmission work.
tasks.still_hard: Whether the future care is acceptable, available and appropriate for this patient.
tasks.human_edge: The nurse hears concerns that a referral form cannot resolve and checks that the plan is understood.
tasks.altitude: Less duplicate handover entry; clinical referral authority and patient-centred planning stay with the existing care team.

reach.task: Check that a receiving service has the actual agreed nursing handover
reach.learn: Provider identity, disclosure boundaries and unresolved care needs

evidence.claim: Exact transfer of existing verified patient fields can reduce duplicate handover entry; this proposed workflow is model knowledge, not a measured nursing result.

assumptions: The focal role is the nurse coordinating an actual authorised transition with a provider handover. The current team plan and any required clinical referral authorisation already exist and are read in s1. This workflow does not grant the nurse new diagnostic or prescribing authority, or treat another clinician's authorisation as free new work.

The existing patient-record producers supply verified patient identifier, contact details, current care orders and relevant medications with timestamps. The nurse verifies the current care context in s1, obtains actual patient preferences in s2 and writes the substantive plan in s4. The service directory and nurse supply and verify exact receiving-provider identity and secure address. No transcript or new structured patient-preference feed is assumed.

s4 removes only 0.98 of fourteen hours for repeated patient/encounter headers; 13.02 retain actual plan writing and correction. s5 removes nine hours of real copying of already verified fields into a separate handover draft. Missing, stale or unsupported fields stop transfer and require manual repair within s6-s7; those full twenty hours retain clinical narrative and meaning checks.

s7 checks exact final content, authority, disclosure scope and provider destination after s6. Any edit invalidates s8 approval. The one-hour secure external send is a real handover; the separate ordinary internal save in s9 is fully retained and ungated. Test the native exchange before code, with clinical data access and local consultation included in rollout.
unknowns: Which fields are actually copied into a separate provider handover?
Can the installed exchange bind final content to a verified provider address?
research_questions: Can an inactive handover draft preserve current clinical context and reject stale data before an exact recipient-bound release?

already_counted.description: Case-specific narrative, clinical meaning checks and failed-transfer manual repair

incremental.description: Maintain handover field mappings and secure provider directory checks

approvals.approved_version: Exact complete handover content, patient identity, disclosure scope and secure receiving-provider address checked in s7; any edit or recipient change voids release

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central removes 0.98 header hours, nine second-entry hours and one actual send hour less 1.5 upkeep: 9.48 net, rounded down. Cautious case: the receiving provider cannot accept the field format and all nine copying hours remain; the native record headers and approved secure send still remove 1.98, less 1.5 upkeep gives 0.48, rounded down to 0.4.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Analyze therapeutic indications, contraindications, risks and cost-benefit trade-offs

steps.what: Read the actual clinical context, current therapies and relevant patient priorities
Locate and read current approved guidance for the actual therapeutic intervention
Analyze indications, contraindications, complications and cost-benefit trade-offs for this patient
Document actual nursing considerations, uncertainties and clinical team questions in the existing record
Save the ordinary nursing analysis in the existing clinical record

tasks.design: Configure direct section links to current approved therapeutic guidance in {DOCS}, alongside the actual record in {OTHER}, the clinical record system. Retain the nurse's full therapeutic analysis and actual record writing; this adds no treatment-selection model or clinical order release.
tasks.previous_blocker: Current guidance may require navigating several document sections before the patient-specific analysis.
tasks.enabler_now: Native document anchors can remove navigation while leaving the source and its applicability visible.
tasks.still_hard: Balancing uncertain benefits and complications against this patient's condition and preferences.
tasks.human_edge: The nurse recognises limitations in both the guidance and the current patient information.
tasks.altitude: Slightly less guidance navigation; therapeutic judgement, prescribing authority and escalation responsibilities stay unchanged.

reach.task: Explain the nursing risks of a proposed intervention
reach.learn: Evidence applicability, uncertainty and multidisciplinary escalation

evidence.claim: Direct links to governed clinical guidance can reduce document navigation without automating therapeutic judgement. This is model knowledge.

assumptions: The focal role is the nurse's actual therapeutic analysis, including the nursing analysis recorded for the clinical team. The task's automate prior does not establish that clinical judgement can be automated. These shares and navigation cuts are E1 estimates.

Current record producers supply patient identifier, current status, relevant results and current therapies; the actual proposing clinician supplies the candidate intervention. The nurse reads these and patient priorities in s1. The protocol owner supplies guidance identifier, version, section and effective date. No extracted patient summary, new diagnostic feed or automatic candidate-treatment generator is assumed.

Only two of twenty guidance hours are repeat navigation to a known relevant section; eighteen retain source reading, applicability checks and broken-link fallback. All forty-five clinical analysis hours and fourteen substantive documentation hours remain. The record write is explicitly outside the reading/decision steps and is not a new trailing analysis registry.

The one-hour same-system save is fully retained and ungated. No prescribing, treatment activation, clinical recommendation send or patient disclosure is performed by this configuration. Existing medication-surveillance runtime is not saved nursing labour. Test native section links before code and retain manual source access when version anchors fail.
unknowns: Are relevant guidance sections already directly linked?
What clinical record entry is actually kept for this analysis?
Which intervention families require evidence beyond the current local protocol?
research_questions: Can native source anchors remain current without encouraging reliance on an inapplicable protocol section?

already_counted.description: Full source reading, applicability checks and broken-link fallback

incremental.description: Verify section links when approved guidance versions change

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central removes two guidance-navigation hours less 0.3 upkeep: 1.7 net. Cautious case: an unusual intervention needs a full new evidence search rather than a known protocol section, or current links already suffice; retain current source access without another link configuration. Clinical analysis and note writing remain fully retained.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Distinguish normal age-related changes from abnormal physiological and behavioural changes in illness

steps.what: Observe and assess the patient's actual physiological and behavioural presentation
Read prior baseline observations and relevant age or developmental history
Distinguish expected variation from abnormal changes using the actual illness context
Record the actual findings, baseline comparison and uncertainty in the existing assessment note
Save the ordinary assessment note in the current patient's clinical record

tasks.design: Configure a native view of existing baseline observations and their dates in {OTHER}, the clinical record system. Keep new assessment, developmental interpretation and substantive assessment writing human; the view does not classify a change as normal or abnormal.
tasks.previous_blocker: Relevant prior baseline entries can sit on different clinical record screens.
tasks.enabler_now: An existing record view can bring already recorded baseline fields together with their provenance.
tasks.still_hard: Determining whether a change reflects illness, development, an individual baseline or missing information.
tasks.human_edge: The nurse integrates direct observation with the patient's and family's account and recognises uncertainty.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated baseline-screen navigation; clinical interpretation and escalation authority remain unchanged.

reach.task: Explain uncertainty in an age-related baseline comparison
reach.learn: Developmental variation, source reliability and acute deterioration pathways

evidence.claim: A governed view can present existing dated baseline observations without making the clinical distinction between normal and abnormal changes. This is model knowledge.

assumptions: The focal role is an actual nursing assessment with its existing clinically used note. Observation in s1 and the first assessment-note write in s4 are separately counted. No new behaviour log or report for every casual observation is invented. Shares and screen-navigation time are provisional E1 estimates.

Prior clinicians already supply patient identifier, observation type, value or narrative, observation date and author in the existing baseline record. The view only presents those fields and timestamps. The nurse obtains current findings directly in s1 and interprets them in s3; no new clean baseline, family transcript, emotion inference or model diagnosis is assumed.

The native view removes two of twenty baseline-access hours spent switching between existing screens; eighteen retain reading, provenance checks and manual retrieval when entries cannot be displayed. All new physical assessment, clinical distinction and substantive writing remain. Missing historical data requires actual patient/family inquiry rather than fabricated normal values.

The ordinary author save is one fully retained ungated hour. Any real urgent escalation remains necessary and must be recorded as its actual call or message, not an automated decision from this view. The configuration performs no clinical alert, diagnosis or treatment release. Test native views before code; data access and national employee consultation are included in rollout.
unknowns: Are dated baseline observations already visible together?
Which age or developmental history is actually documented?
How often are prior findings unavailable or unreliable?
research_questions: Does the view preserve observation dates and uncertainty without presenting stale history as the current patient baseline?

already_counted.description: Baseline reading, provenance checks and manual retrieval fallback

incremental.description: Verify baseline-view field and timestamp mappings after record changes

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central removes two baseline-screen navigation hours less 0.4 upkeep: 1.6 net. Cautious case: baseline history exists only in unstructured external notes or is absent, so the native fields cannot supply a useful view; retain actual manual retrieval and inquiry without deploying this view or adding upkeep. Current assessment and clinical interpretation do not change.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Retain clinical and teaching judgement while reducing actual formatting and duplicate coordination fields.
role.ambitious_version: An acute care nurse with less repeated documentation and unchanged accountability for clinical care.
